subject: Hybrid session token-flooring: proposed math & examples
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Billing model math for our hybrid use

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough. Two follow-ups from our end as we build the internal cost model: we expect ~250k gen calls/month, ~40% of those will be long-chat (context ~= 8k-16k tokens), and the rest are short assistant calls (~128 tokens).

Can you confirm how billing rounds for these hybrid sessions? Specifically:
- Do you round generation/token billing to a fixed quantum (e.g., 64 tokens), or is it per-token for long contexts?
- Is there an active-session floor (per hour or per call) that would affect bursty traffic?
- How do KV cache re-uses within the same session get credited (do we pay again for repeated prefixes)?

Attached is an initial usage spreadsheet. We also need to understand how committed discounts would interact with any per-session minimums — some of our procurement folks push back on per-call floors if they drive higher unit costs on net.

Appreciate a short worked example (math) so we can put numbers in our procurement doc.

Samir
Acme Corp — Sr. PM

Attachment: acme_usage_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-03-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing model math for our hybrid use

Samir — thanks for the clear breakdown. Quick answers up front, then a short worked example below. Looping Ben and Vanessa for discount/contract and accounting detail.

Short answers:
- Rounding: generation tokens are charged in quanta. For our generation SKU we use a 64-token quantum for pricing (i.e., billed tokens = ceil(tokens/64)*64). Embedding calls use a 16-token quantum.
- Session floor: we do not bill a "per-hour" flat fee by default, but we apply a small active-session floor to prevent pathological micro-calls from creating excessive overheads: 1,024 token-equivalent per active session per hour. That only applies if you have continuous open sessions that otherwise would bill below that threshold.
- KV cache: repeated use of cached prefixes within an active session is not re-billed as new prompt tokens; only the delta tokens beyond the cached prefix are billed.

Worked example (month with mixed call lengths):
- Short calls: 150k calls at 128 tokens each -> billed per-call quantum: 128 tokens -> 128 tokens * 150k = 19,200,000 billed tokens.
- Long-chat: 100k calls average 8,500 tokens per call -> per-call billed = ceil(8500/64)*64 = 8,512 -> 8,512 * 100k = 851,200,000 billed tokens.
- Session-floor: if you have 2k concurrently active sessions that are idle for 30 minutes and would otherwise bill <1,024 tokens in that hour, they would be billed up to the 1,024 tokens threshold for that hour.

I've attached a quick CSV with the math (rough_cost_calc.csv). Ben / Vanessa — suggested approach for a committed discount: provide a blended per-token discount on billed tokens (post-quantum rounding) with a "floor credit" cap — i.e., credits for session-floor charges limited to X% of monthly committed spend. Happy to model numbers.

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rough_cost_calc.csv (CSV with example rows)

Subject: Re: Billing model math for our hybrid use

Samir / Naomi — quick commercial proposal to make procurement happy while keeping unit economics intact.

Proposal highlights:
- Pricing primitives (post-quantum billing): generation billed at $0.00006 / billed token, embedding at $0.00002 / billed token. (These are examples for modeling; final pricing to be set in SOW.)
- Discount tiers by committed monthly billed tokens (post-rounding):
  - >= 200M billed tokens: 8% discount
  - >= 500M billed tokens: 15% discount
  - >= 1B billed tokens: 22% discount
- Session-floor handling: we will credit session-floor charges back as "floor credits" up to 5% of committed monthly spend in a pilot period (first 3 months). After pilot, session-floor credits reduce to a negotiated cap. This prevents unchecked floor abuse while keeping billing predictable.
- Rounding differential mitigation: for long-chat heavy customers we can offer an alternate quantum of 32 tokens (instead of 64) for the generation SKU if the majority (>60%) of calls are long-chat and we get a 12-month commit. This lowers rounding inefficiency for you.

Example blended math (apply to Naomi's numbers):
- Billed tokens total from Naomi's calc = ~870.4M. At 15% discount (500M tier) effective rate = $0.000051 / token -> estimated monthly bill ~$44.4k before floor credits.

Next steps: Naomi to share a quick SOW sketch; Vanessa to confirm how floor credits will appear on invoice and the mechanics for a cap.

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales
